source.title: Concepts Whisper: Spectral Anti-Concentration and the Dual Geometry of Transformer Representations
source.authors: Pratyush Acharya; Nuraj Rimal; H. Dhakal

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition as a possible capacity interpretation, but its experiments measure spectral placement of concept directions, not feature overlap, capacity competition, sparsity-dependent transitions, or the other listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on spectral anti-concentration and related representation geometry; these findings are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure what any listed version specifies. Its steering and POS-probing experiments concern effects of spectral subspaces, not superposition or the listed versions. WCA transport results are not included because they do not measure the claim's subject. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures where concept directions sit in the unembedding-covariance eigenspectrum, using a Gini deviation and spectral center of mass. It uses existing Gemma Scope and Llama Scope SAE decoder columns as one of three ways to extract concept directions, so it treats SAE features as concept units without testing whether they are. Superposition comes up only in the Discussion, as a speculative capacity reading: the authors argue that if syntax claims the high-variance head, effective dimensionality is much smaller than d, which would force superposition. None of its results measure feature overlap or interference in toy models, polysemanticity, capacity competition, SAE recovery or completeness, or feature dimensionality. The reader's 'discusses/T6' is defensible, but 'uses_without_test/T4' better describes the SAE usage.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that word-level concept directions robustly occupy the spectrally quiet subspace across 17 models and three extraction methods, and that static unembedding contrasts do the opposite. They also conclude that cross-lingual transport via the causal inner product (WCA) gives no benefit beyond spectral regularization. They call the functional claim that the high-variance subspace carries syntactic load 'supported but not settled'. They offer the link to superposition only as a candidate mechanism, without testing it.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures spectral geometry in pretrained language models using concept directions, SAE features, probes, and unembedding contrasts. It does not train toy networks with sparse features or test the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports variation by model, SAE feature-selection setting, covariance construction, and spectral cutoff; anti-concentration remains negative across its reported covariance variants and cutoffs. These findings do not test the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Difference-of-means concept directions anti-concentrate in the low-variance tail of the unembedding second-moment spectrum in all 17 models. They are more tail-aligned than norm-matched random directions in 13 of 17.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contextualized word-level concept directions occupy low-variance directions of the unembedding spectrum, beyond what anisotropy alone produces.

fits_no_version.finding: The same sign appears for an expanded set of semantic concepts, for pretrained SAE decoder directions, and for linear probes. Probes failed on Gemma-2-9b.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral anti-concentration of concept directions holds across several extraction methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Static unembedding-row contrasts for concept pairs concentrate in high-variance directions, more than random token-pair contrasts do (p<1e-4, four models).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Static vocabulary contrasts and activation-space concept directions occupy opposite ends of the spectrum (a dual geometry).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper's evidence concerns word-level counterfactual concepts and a spectrum derived from the unembedding matrix, not direct feature overlap or capacity competition. SAE and probe evidence covers a limited subset of models; the paper reports probe failure on Gemma-2-9b. The paper itself identifies its word-level concept scope and notes that abstract and discourse-level concepts remain untested.
record.rows_left_out: Steering and POS-probing results in Section 8 and Tables 5, 6, and 12–15 were not included: they measure spectral-subspace effects on perplexity or syntactic-tag prediction, not any listed version of the superposition claim. WCA transport results in Section 4 were also excluded as unrelated to the claim's measured subject.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparse-feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent phase transition, or regular polytope geometry.

There is no neuron-level polysemanticity measure and no test of capacity competition. The capacity account appears only as a discussion hypothesis linking a reduced effective dimension to superposition.
No examination of non-capacity causes of polysemantic neurons.
Pretrained SAE features are used as given. Neither the spread of features across neurons nor the quality of SAE recovery is measured.
No test of the completeness, stability, or canonicity of SAE features. The feature-collapse analysis concerns concept-to-feature mapping, not SAE stability.
Multi-dimensional features (Engels et al.) are cited only. No comparison of 1-D and multi-D features.

record.verdict_notes: The record's exclusion of the steering, POS-probing, and WCA results is appropriate, since none of them bears on any version. The superposition link appears only in the Discussion (Section 9) as an untested hypothesis, so no verdict labels are given. The changed relation and tranche reflect the use of pretrained SAE features as concept units without testing them.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
No test of neurons sharing features because of capacity pressure, or of important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.
The paper uses existing SAE features and measures their spectral placement, but does not test feature recovery or whether real-model features spread across neurons.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional and multidimensional features as units of superposition.

rows.subject: 17-model core suite (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Gini deviation of difference-of-means concept directions against the uniform spectral baseline.
rows.measure: Mean Gini deviation; one-sample test across models
rows.value: Mean Gini deviation −0.282; all 17 models negative; t = −11.5, p = 3.8 × 10−9, n = 17
rows.note: Measures spectral anti-concentration, not superposition or feature overlap.

rows.subject: 17-model core suite (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared concept directions with norm-matched random directions in the same eigenbasis.
rows.measure: True-minus-null Gini gap; models with greater concept tail alignment
rows.value: Mean true-minus-null Gini gap −0.082; concept directions more tail-aligned in 13 of 17 models
rows.note: The paper names Llama 3.2 (1B and 3B), Mistral-7B-v0.3, and OLMoE as exceptions.
